column1: # rank-vectors.tsv — test vectors for the magnitude-head rank scheme.
# queue.py, beside this file, is the only implementation that runs these. A Go
# one was drafted and never merged, so no second suite checks these vectors.
# The fixture holds its value regardless, because that value was never a second
# consumer. Every expected key here is derived from the scheme's rules — a head
# letter fixing the integer part's length, base-36 digits, plain string
# comparison as the order — rather than read off a run. Vectors taken from a run
# prove only that the run agrees with itself; vectors derived from the rules can
# contradict the implementation, which is what this file is for.
# Tab-separated columns: lo, hi, want, note.
#   lo, hi  the neighbours the new key goes between; "-" means open-ended
#   want    the key the scheme requires, or "!" when the call must fail
#   note    what the case is for
# A runner must also check that the result orders strictly between lo and hi,
# which catches a wrong expectation here as well as a wrong implementation.
# The cases sit where the two could drift rather than where they agree easily:
# magnitude-head boundaries, a magnitude exhausted between adjacent keys, and
